Title: Aliza's true calling
NewsSummary: Aliza Hussain received the Best Graduate Award from the Medical College at the Aga Khan University's 27th Convocation Ceremony in Karachi.

content.text: Aliza Hussain received the Best Graduate Award from the Medical College at the Aga Khan University's 27th Convocation Ceremony in Karachi. Hussain currently works as a teaching associate in the biological and biomedical sciences department at AKU.

Honestly, I was undecided about medicine even after I got into AKU. My mom who works as an assistant professor in the community health sciences department at AKU and has been actively involved in many public health projects over the years, and my dad who recently retired from the Navy, had a firm belief that I'd do well in the profession and told me to pursue it. But for me it was not until I started medical school that I fell in love with the profession.

I still remember the first two years of medicine, learning more and more about the human body, from the intricate anatomy of the human brain, to the flawless heart working at a perfect rhythm, and then in the clinical years, being able to put the same knowledge into practice. Actually, it was not one moment, not one person and not one lesson. In fact it was this whole, living, breathing institution that just reaffirmed my faith that this was my true calling.

One of the most important lessons I learnt at AKU was to lead by example. It's as simple as that. My teachers didn't preach with words but showed each one of us in practical terms how doctors can bring about change. Simple acts of kindness and honest medical practice is all it takes to help people. Access to primary health care is a basic human right that we many-a-times overlook and shy away from. AKU teaches the importance of just that. I learnt that medicine isn't just a profession but a life choice, and I have seen in my five years here that truly dedicated medical professionals, not just clinicians, but hospital administration and staff, can help improve many lives.

Whether it was the inspiration from our professors and faculty who taught us, the competent clinicians with whom we did our rounds, the helpful residents and even the cooperative patients whom we attended to at the clinics, every person I met at AKU inspired me to want to do better. I learnt from their experiences and felt a sense of pride about this profession. That is the beauty of this institution. In my five years here the faculty effortlessly guided me into the practical realm of medicine - something very few medical universities are able to do.

I can easily state that today I am proud to join the league of great professionals that AKU prides itself in graduating. Looking back at my days spent at the University, I remember my favourite rotations of ENT in third year and internal medicine in the fifth year. They were the most structured and well planned out rotations. We were expected to play an active role in patient care and take responsibility of our patients. Here we gained hands-on experience. By the end of the rotations I felt like an actual contributing member of the team. That's the kind of medical knowledge that no book can teach anyone but only AKU can.
